newsitem.title: USA: N.C. Democrats ask ethics panel to probe Helms.
newsitem.headline: N.C. Democrats ask ethics panel to probe Helms.

text.p: The North Carolina Democratic Party called Thursday for a U.S. Senate investigation of Republican Sen. Jesse Helms, charging he had falsified financial records about his rental properties.

The complaint to the U.S. Senate Ethics Committee says Helms failed to list in a May financial disclosure statement at least six rental properties and thus understated the collective value of his property by more than $500,000.
The properties are decrepit and have been the scene of drug-related activities and violence, according to a statement from state Democratic Party Chairman Lisbeth Evans.
"The failure to disclose may have been a deliberate attempt to hide the fact that the senator is a millionaire slumlord," she said.

The charges come as Helms, a conservative icon who has represented North Carolina in the Senate for 24 years, battles architect and former Charlotte, North Carolina, mayor Harvey Gantt in a rematch bid for the Senate seat.
Voters will take their pick at the polls Nov. 5.

Evans, in a letter Thursday to Sen. Mitch McConnell, chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Ethics, said Helms had violated the federal false statements statute and might be subject to civil and criminal penalties.
"Senator Helms portrays himself as a champion of the average person, and he would, therefore, have every incentive to cover up the fact that he is a millionaire," she said.
The complaint followed reports in Thursday's edition of the News & Observer newspaper in Raleigh, North Carolina.
Helms was said to own 15 rental properties valued at $1.3 million instead of the nine he reported.
The North Carolina Democratic Party released copies of Helms' U.S. Senate Public Financial Disclosure reports showing nine rental properties valued at between $250,000 and $500,000.

"But Wake County Tax and Property Records show that the senator and his wife own 15 rental properties which have a tax-assessed value of over one million dollars," Evans said. "Helms lied about the number and value of his rental properties. ..."
Wake County Tax and Property Records officials were not available, and Helms campaign aides did not return calls.
By law, U.S. senators are required to report sources of unearned income for themselves and their wives.
"This is not about a simple clerical error. This is about lying to the Senate Ethics Committee," Evans' letter said.
She said Helms had also underreported the number of properties in his last battle against Gantt, in 1990.
